## Executive summary

I led the analysis behind a major subscription pricing initiative. Rather than treating pricing as a single revenue decision, I evaluated how pricing options could support customers at each stage, from adoption to paid conversion and account expansion.

## Business challenge

A subscription-based digital advertising product sought to improve customer progression from adoption to paid conversion and account expansion. I evaluated opportunities to support sustainable subscription growth through customer analytics and pricing strategy.

## My role

- Owned the analytical strategy end to end, partnering with Product, Sales, and Finance
- Built the behavioral segmentation and lifecycle funnel analysis
- Developed the pricing scenario framework and presented recommendations to product and commercial leadership
- Supported go-to-market rollout with dashboards for Sales and Product

## Analytical approach

I analyzed lifecycle behavior and merchant segments, then assessed alternative pricing scenarios against adoption and revenue objectives. Instead of asking only *"how much should we charge?"*, I asked **"how does each pricing option affect customers' progress through the lifecycle?"**

**How I compare pricing trade-offs**

[Illustrative framework]{.provenance .provenance-illustrative}

| Hypothetical scenario | Conversion potential | Revenue sustainability | Implementation complexity |
|---|---|---|---|
| A · Simple price adjustment | Medium | Low | Low |
| B · Segment-targeted offer | High | Medium | High |
| C · Packaging redesign | Medium | High | Medium |

[Illustrative decision framework: the scenarios and ratings are invented to show the method. They are not LINE's actual pricing options, rules, or results.]{.illustrative}

No option wins on every dimension, which is the point of the exercise: the matrix makes the trade-offs explicit so that stakeholders can decide against shared objectives.

## Outcome

- Contributed to a major subscription pricing initiative supporting stronger paid-customer growth and business performance
- Helped frame the leadership discussion around the full customer lifecycle as well as immediate revenue
- Dashboards helped Sales and Product support the rollout
- The analysis became the foundation for a later [KPI reporting automation project](../line-kpi-reporting-automation/index.qmd)

## Lessons learned

- **Judge pricing across the lifecycle.** An option can look different once its effect on later stages is considered alongside immediate revenue.
- **Segment before you decide.** Different customer groups can respond differently to the same pricing option.
- **Plan for the rollout.** Giving Sales and Product the right view of customers is part of making a pricing change work.
